We need to count palindromes of exactly n digits and the total below 10^n.

For n digits, the first half (ceil(n/2)) can be any digit 0–9, so 10^(ceil(n/2)) choices.
The second half is a mirror, so no extra choices.
Thus palindromes of exactly n digits = 10^(ceil(n/2)).

Total below 10^n = sum over all shorter lengths:
  1-digit: 9 (1–9)
  2-digit: 9 (11–99)
  …
  n-digit: 10^(ceil(n/2))
So total = 9 + 9 + … + 10^(ceil(n/2)) = 9*(n–1) + 10^(ceil(n/2)).
